**[WARNING]:** Optional `$VerificationReceipt` crashes the script when omitted — `.Replace()` on a null string

`[string]$VerificationReceipt` (line 8) is non-mandatory and binds to `$null` when not supplied, so line 14's `$VerificationReceipt.Replace('\','/')` throws `You cannot call a method on a null-valued expression` — a terminating error under `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. The documented `local-fixture` scope never reads the receipt (release_smoke.sh:24–28 consults it only for `trusted-candidate`), so that documented path on Windows is unusable. Guard the parameter or coerce it before calling `.Replace()`.

---
Reply with `@kilocode-bot fix it` to have Kilo Code address this issue.

> **[WARNING]:** Optional `$VerificationReceipt` crashes the script when omitted — `.Replace()` on a null string

I reproduced omission with actual PowerShell 7.5.4: an optional [string] parameter binds to an empty string, and .Replace succeeds. The proposed null crash does not occur, so this line is unchanged. This binder probe is separate from the still-pending native Windows terminal acceptance.
